subject.title: fix(exec-approvals): handle same-process sync/async lock contention

question: Must an exec authorization read remain linearized behind an in-flight same-process policy revocation, or may it intentionally use the last committed policy until that write finishes?
rationale: The PR chooses availability over revocation freshness inside an authorization boundary; repository source currently documents and implements serialized reads, so changing that contract needs an explicit owner decision.

options.title: Preserve revocation serialization
options.body: Refactor the contending runtime path to use the async lock or a committed snapshot so synchronous readers never bypass an in-flight policy update.

options.title: Accept last-committed reads
options.body: Explicitly permit stale same-process reads, document the authorization window, and prove restrictive updates plus Windows fallback behavior before merge.

recommendation.title: Preserve revocation serialization
recommendation.body: Refactor the contending runtime path to use the async lock or a committed snapshot so synchronous readers never bypass an in-flight policy update.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest available recent exec-approval routing candidate, though direct lock-history ownership remains unconfirmed.
